source.title: ISO 15765-2 normal fixed addressing and the ISO 15765-4 test equipment address
source.origin: ISO 15765-2:2016, Road vehicles — Diagnostic communication over CAN, Part 2, normal fixed addressing (11-bit/29-bit CAN identifier mapping); ISO 15765-4:2016, Part 4, requirements for emissions-related systems, external test equipment source address
source.provenance: Standards facts restated by the project; the standards themselves are not redistributed
source.notes: Two facts only: how a 29-bit normal-fixed identifier is composed, and that ISO 15765-4 assigns 0xF1 to external test equipment. Whether JLR's enhanced diagnostics accept 0xF1 is a separate, research-class claim.

locator.description: ISO 15765-2:2016, normal fixed addressing, 29-bit CAN identifier: priority and PDU format in the upper bits (0x18DA for physical, 0x18DB for functional target addressing), target address N_TA in bits 15..8, source address N_SA in bits 7..0; a response carries the addresses swapped

evidence.excerpt: request = prefix << 16 | N_TA << 8 | N_SA; response = prefix << 16 | N_SA << 8 | N_TA

locator.description: ISO 15765-4:2016, external test equipment source address for legislated OBD over CAN with normal fixed addressing

evidence.excerpt: N_SA of the external test equipment = 0xF1
evidence.notes: Stated for legislated OBD. Its use for JLR enhanced diagnostics is the research hypothesis recorded separately.
